newsitem.title: JAPAN: US Treasuries lower in Tokyo, supply concerns grow.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries lower in Tokyo, supply concerns grow.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries fell further by Tokyo midday on Thursday, carrying over the bearish mood from the New York trade.
"Follow-through selling depressed prices this morning," a Japanese brokerage trader said. "There were more offers lined up this morning following sharp falls overnight."
Traders said concerns over fresh supplies were hurting market sentiment. Several Treasury auctions are scheduled for next week, including two- and five-year note sales.
"Prices should be capped until we see the results of the auctions next week," the trader said.
The 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond stood at 95-22/32, yielding 6.97 percent, compared with 95-25/32 in New York.
The June T-bond futures contract was unchanged at 109-9/32 from the previous close.
In New York, longer-end prices closed sharply lower on hedge fund selling. The market was also concerned about March U.S. trade data which showed the economy continuing to grow.
Traders said many operators refrained from trading in large volumes this morning, as Japanese investors continued to be sidelined and to cautiously watch movements of the dollar.
